description: Deterministic PRELIMINARY ICP (Ideal Customer Profile) qualification rules for the master prospect store. Pure rule-based text matching against fields that genuinely exist in data/master/master.json (business name, category/type, website presence, rating, review_count, address/city/state/country, employee_count if present) -- no AI/LLM calls, no enrichment, no invented fields (no revenue, capacity, or true commercial specialization data, since this layer does not and cannot know those with certainty from currently-available fields). This layer produces a preliminary status/confidence/score; final ICP qualification requires later website/business enrichment that does not exist yet in this repo.

hard_exclusions.description: Any single match forces tier D regardless of positive signals. Matched case-insensitively against business_name + category text.

single_trade_only_keywords.description: Business names/categories indicating a single non-HVAC trade with no HVAC signal present are excluded -- these are not HVAC contractors at all.

residential_only_exclusion.description: Residential-only HVAC (no commercial signal anywhere in name/category) is excluded to tier D. Mixed residential+commercial is NOT excluded and scores normally.

strong_commercial_service_signals.description: Keywords in business_name/category providing DIRECT evidence that the business itself is a commercial-focused HVAC/mechanical service provider. These are the only keywords capable of producing icp_confidence 'high' on their own (tagged icp_evidence 'commercial_hvac_signal', or 'industrial_signal' for the industrial-specific ones). Additive points, matched independently (a record may match several).

mechanical_contractor_signal.description: 'mechanical contractor'/'mechanical contractors' is direct-but-ambiguous: it only counts as strong DIRECT commercial evidence (icp_evidence 'commercial_service_signal', contributes to icp_confidence 'high') when combined with a general HVAC signal elsewhere in the text -- otherwise 'mechanical contractor' alone could mean plumbing/other trades and is not treated as direct HVAC evidence.

commercial_customer_vertical_signals.description: Keywords indicating the business serves commercial verticals (customer-side signal, distinct from the provider being commercial-branded). Additive points.

general_hvac_signal.description: Baseline recognition that the record is an HVAC/mechanical business at all (before commercial/residential qualifiers). Applied once.

bonus_signals.description: Secondary evidence-based bonuses. Every check only fires when the underlying field is actually populated on the record -- never fabricated.

has_website.description: Website present -- proxy for an established, findable business.

rating_at_least.description: Google rating >= 4.0, only scored when rating is present.

review_count_at_least.description: Review count >= 10, only scored when review_count is present.

review_count_at_least_high.description: Additional bonus for review_count >= 50 (stacks with the >=10 bonus), only scored when present.

employee_count_present.description: Employee/size data is NEVER required and NEVER fabricated. If a future master record happens to carry an 'employee_count' or 'employees' field (not produced by the current collection pipeline), it is used only as a bonus, never as a qualification requirement.

confidence_rules.description: icp_confidence is driven ONLY by direct keyword evidence (strong_commercial_service_signals / mechanical_contractor_signal / commercial_customer_vertical_signals / general_hvac_signal matches). Generic secondary bonuses (website, rating, review_count, employee_count) can NEVER by themselves produce 'high' or upgrade 'low' to 'medium' -- they may only be reported as supporting icp_evidence tags alongside a keyword-derived confidence.
confidence_rules.high: At least one strong_commercial_service_signals keyword matched, OR mechanical_contractor_signal matched together with a general_hvac_signal match.
confidence_rules.medium: general_hvac_signal matched AND at least one commercial_customer_vertical_signals keyword matched, but no 'high' condition met.
confidence_rules.low: Anything else (no signal, or only a general_hvac_signal match with no vertical signal, or only bonus signals).

status_rules.description: icp_status is the PRIMARY downstream decision. icp_tier remains a secondary, transparent numeric classification.
status_rules.excluded: Any hard exclusion or residential-only exclusion matched.
status_rules.qualified: No exclusion, AND (icp_confidence == 'high' OR (icp_confidence == 'medium' AND icp_score >= qualified_min_score_for_medium_confidence)).
status_rules.review: No exclusion, and the 'qualified' condition is not met -- potentially relevant but current evidence is insufficient to confidently qualify. This is an EXPECTED, intentional outcome, not a failure of the record or the rules.

insufficient_evidence_penalty.description: Records with almost no signal at all (no HVAC-relevant category text, no website, no rating/review data) are capped so they cannot reach A/A+ purely on the base score.

notes: Scoring is purely additive/subtractive over base_score using the sections above; no field is invented that isn't already in data/master/master.json.

Hard exclusions and the residential-only exclusion both force tier D and icp_status 'excluded' by setting an icp_excluded flag that overrides the numeric tier lookup, but the numeric score is still computed and reported for transparency.
All keyword matching is case-insensitive substring matching over business_name and category text -- deterministic, no fuzzy/AI matching.

This is a PRELIMINARY qualification layer only. It cannot know true revenue, capacity, or commercial specialization with certainty -- it only reasons over currently-available Google Maps/master-store fields. Final ICP qualification requires later website/business enrichment not built in this repo.
